definition: Deplete means to reduce greatly the amount or supply of something; to use up.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word deplete. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know deplete should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By February the flu season had depleted the district's roster of fill-in teachers.
A dent is the first bite out of a stock — noticeable, and nothing more — far short of deplete, which reports the level drawn down toward empty.
Exhaust goes further than deplete — a depleted well still gives some water; an exhausted one gives none at all.

To drain is to draw a supply down the way liquid leaves a tank — and a drain can run all the way to empty. Deplete reports the level falling sharply without saying the tank is dry: harvests deplete soil, spending sprees deplete savings. Drain is the picture; deplete is the accountant's report.

To sap is to bleed strength away little by little — energy, morale, resolve. Deplete aims at stock instead of strength: supplies, savings, reserves, a roster. A long fever saps a patient; a long winter can deplete the woodpile.
